Even though we have a requirement of 100 comment contribution points to unlock the ability to downvote comments, people have started to abuse this by engaging in serial downvoting of all comments (witch-hunting) submitted by a specific person. This was brought to my attention and I personally examined a few downvoted comments. These comments had no valid reason to be downvoted whatsoever because they contributed to a discussion they were submitted to and they followed the well known code of conduct (known as reddiquette on that other site).

I then proceeded to examine the voting history of the serial downvoter and found over 200 negative votes directed more or less towards a single account.

While it is in my power to ban this person, revert their downvotes or even convert them to upvotes, I would like to get the input from whoaverse community on how we should deal with issues like this one in a transparent and civilized way.

Some users suggested building a system where each downvote would cost the downvoter x comment points or where we would throttle downvoting (allow 1 downvote per x minutes), shadowban the offenders, make their voting history public etc.

Please help us make whoaverse a better place by giving us your (REALISTIC) ideas on how to tackle this problem and prevent it from happening in the future or how to at least minimize the effects of such behavior.

Thank you!
